lesson.title: Rebasing a Feature Branch and Resolving Conflicts in Git
lesson.goal: rebase a feature branch onto main with git and resolve the conflicts

goalMatch.note: This video covers exactly how to rebase a branch onto main and walks through resolving conflicts with a worked example.

sources.title: Rebasing a Feature Branch and Resolving Conflicts in Git

steps.title: Set up repository and check branches
steps.instructions: Initialize a Git repo with index.js and package.json, create diverging commits on main and a feature branch that edit the same lines in both files, then check out the feature branch. Run git branch -a to confirm your feature branch is local and safe to rebase.

precision_checks.label: Branches have diverged
precision_checks.command: test "$(git rev-list --count HEAD..main)" -ge 1 && test "$(git rev-list --count main..HEAD)" -ge 1

targets.caption: Confirm your feature branch is checked out
git branch -a lists local branches only, no remotes/origin

explanations.topic: Why rebase creates a linear commit history
How git rebase replays commits onto a new base
Golden rule: never rebase pushed commits
Checking pushed branches with git branch -a

hints: Make sure both main and your feature branch have commits modifying the same lines in index.js and package.json.
Switch to your feature branch before checking branches or rebasing.
Run git branch -a and confirm there is no remotes/origin entry for your feature branch.
common_mistakes: Rebasing a branch that has already been pushed and shared with teammates
Running git branch -a while still checked out on main
steps.code: git init -b main && echo 'const DEFAULT_USER = "john";' > index.js && echo '{"scripts":{"check":"node -c index.js"}}' > package.json && git add . && git commit -m 'Initial' && git checkout -b feature/login && echo 'const DEFAULT_USER = "admin";' > index.js && git commit -am 'Add login' && echo '{"scripts":{"check":"node --check index.js"}}' > package.json && git commit -am 'Add auth' && git checkout main && echo 'const DEFAULT_USER = "guest";' > index.js && echo '{"scripts":{"check":"node -c index.js --strict"}}' > package.json && git commit -am 'Update main' && git checkout feature/login && git branch -a

steps.title: Start the rebase onto main
steps.instructions: Run git rebase main from your feature branch to replay your commits on top of main. When Git pauses on the first conflict, run git status to inspect the rebase progress.

targets.caption: Git pauses the rebase and reports the first conflicting file

explanations.topic: Reading and resolving conflict markers in index.js

hints: Which command replays your current branch commits onto another branch?
Ensure you are on your feature branch and pass main as the target to git rebase.
Run git rebase main, then run git status to see which file is marked both modified.
common_mistakes: Running git rebase feature/login while on main instead of rebasing onto main
Aborting immediately on the conflict error instead of inspecting git status

steps.title: Resolve and stage index.js conflicts
steps.instructions: Open index.js in your editor, remove all conflict markers, and keep the code you want. Stage it with git add index.js and run git status to verify the conflict is marked fixed.

targets.caption: Remove the conflict markers and choose the final code in index.js
Confirm index.js is staged and ready for git rebase --continue

hints: Look for <<<<<<<, =======, and >>>>>>> lines inside index.js.
Delete the conflict markers, keep the code you want, and save index.js.
Run git add index.js and check git status for the all conflicts fixed message.
common_mistakes: Leaving <<<<<<< or >>>>>>> conflict markers inside index.js
Running git commit instead of staging the resolved file with git add

steps.title: Continue rebase to next commit
steps.instructions: Run git rebase --continue and save the commit message in Vim (Esc, :wq, Enter). Git applies the resolved commit and pauses again on the next conflicting commit, or finishes if none remain.

targets.caption: Git applies the commit and pauses on the next conflict

explanations.topic: Setting VSCode as default git editor

hints: Do not run git commit; use the rebase continuation command shown by git status.
Run git rebase --continue to resume applying commits.
When the commit message opens in Vim, press Esc, type :wq, and press Enter.
common_mistakes: Running git commit instead of git rebase --continue
Getting stuck in Vim without saving and quitting (:wq)

steps.title: Resolve package.json and finish rebase
steps.instructions: Remove the conflict markers in the conflicting file (package.json in the tutorial), stage it with git add, and run git rebase --continue. Then run git status to confirm the rebase finished and the working tree is clean.

precision_checks.label: No rebase in progress
precision_checks.command: test ! -d "$(git rev-parse --git-path rebase-merge)" && test ! -d "$(git rev-parse --git-path rebase-apply)"

targets.caption: Remove conflict markers and keep valid JSON
Rebase finished; git status shows clean tree

explanations.topic: Verifying rebase completion with git status

hints: Edit package.json to remove the conflict markers and ensure valid JSON.
Stage package.json with git add package.json before continuing.
Run git rebase --continue, exit Vim with :wq, and verify with git status.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to stage package.json before running git rebase --continue
Leaving invalid JSON syntax after deleting conflict markers
steps.code: git add package.json && git rebase --continue && git status
